target_customer: Independent hotels in Mexico and the Caribbean (later US and Europe) that pay OTA commissions
problem: Independent hotels pay OTAs 15 to 40 percent commissions and lack tools to sell directly online. GuruHotel gave them a direct booking website and engine at a lower fee.
business_model: Commission on direct bookings (5 percent per Bloomberg Linea coverage) plus platform fees

founders.name: Josué Gio
founders.background_notes: YC page says he is a co-founder and an angel investor in more than 40 LATAM startups.

founders.name: Stiven Martinez
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a digital product designer in Medellin who leads frontend development.

founders.name: Jorge Flores Acevedo
founders.background_notes: YC page describes 10+ years in hotel e-commerce, revenue management and distribution. Bloomberg Linea snippets name only Gio and Martinez, so his founder status rests on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A website builder, booking engine and payments layer for hotels is standard SaaS engineering, with harder parts in integrating with property management systems.

defensibility.rationale: Hotels that route bookings and payments through the platform face some switching cost, but website and booking engine products were already common and the founders cite no proprietary data.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: OTAs remained the dominant channel the product tried to displace. No incumbent copy or acquisition was found.

market_need_then: Hotels paid OTA commissions of about 15 to 40 percent (Bloomberg Linea Dec 2021). The pandemic hit shortly after the batch, and a pre-seed reportedly kept the company alive.

identity.mascot_or_character: Guru, the name of the AI assistant that runs the direct channel (current site)
identity.visual_style: Elegant minimal sample hotel sites with serif typography (current site)
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, short statements such as 'Real hotels. Real revenue.'

branding.brand_signature: Pitch of becoming the Shopify of hotels (Bloomberg Linea, Skift headlines)

brand_strength.rationale: Press covers the funding and Shopify for hotels pitch, but the name is close to other 'guru' travel brands such as Hoteliers.Guru and no community or brand coverage was found.

outcome_analysis: GuruHotel went through YC in early 2020, survived the pandemic on a small pre-seed, raised a $2.1M seed in December 2021 led by Anthemis and reported around 160 hotels. It is listed as active with a team of 12 and now repositions as AI native direct booking infrastructure, but no later round or exit was found, so growth since 2021 is unverified.
notes: Seed amount and Anthemis lead are stated by Skift, Bloomberg Linea, Phocuswire and Contxto per search results; the Skift body I opened lists Anthemis, Magic Fund and 500 Startups only, and Y Combinator comes from search coverage. A $550K pre-seed appears in one search snippet and is not recorded as a round. Aggregator totals conflict ($2.33M, $2.79M, $3.2M). One source says the company launched in Mexico in July 2019. Competitor list is empty: no source dated near March 2020 was found; Skift 2021 and company sites name OTAs and PMS firms but those are not dated at founding. The company site claims 1,000+ hotels, a company figure.
